name: Stage 24:1: Vilsta, Eskilstuna to Hållsta
description: Official Sörmlandsleden stage 24:1, Vilsta, Eskilstuna to Hållsta.
utilities: Vilsta is the strong service/access start, with bus line 6 context from Eskilstuna, parking near Vilsta raststuga, toilets, designated grill places, lodging/camping, restaurant/cafe context, and nearby bathing facilities.

Skjulsta is a side-trip/access service cluster about 400 m from the trail, with parking, cafe, toilets, grill places, bathing, exercise tracks and Uvberget access. Treat it as a detour/service cluster, not an on-route facility line.
No official shelter, dependable on-stage toilet, or reliable mid-stage drinking water was verified between the Vilsta/Skjulsta service area and Hållsta.

Hållsta endpoint has no official parking at the stage start. The nearest bus context is Åläng/Hållsta village to the west/northwest; current public maps show line 19 Hållsta-Bälgviken and night bus 65, while older Sörmlandsleden text may still mention bus 9. Hållsta badplats is an off-route village facility with toilet, grill and bathing context, not a guaranteed trailhead service.
waterSources: The only official natural water point is the Piltorp/Dalkarlstorp spring, but the official page says it is not accessible as of a 2025-05 report. Mark it as unavailable and do not rely on it until reverified.

Carry drinking water from Vilsta/Eskilstuna or from verified staffed services. Surface water around Skjulsta/Eskilstunaån and Hållsta badplats is natural/untested and should not be presented as drinking water.
notes: Sörmlandsleden does not guarantee water quality or availability; treat or filter natural sources and carry backup.
Shelters are generally free, shared, first-come, cannot be booked, and do not guarantee firewood or trash service.
In nature reserves, local camping and fire rules override allemansrätten; fires are often restricted to prepared fireplaces.

Official and Naturkartan distance is 12 km. OSM relation 9631287 is the correct Stage 24:1 relation and measures about 11.4 km; AllTrails around 10.9 km, RouteYou around 8 km and Äventyrligare around 15 km should not replace the official display distance.

Draw Stage 24:1 as a standalone Vilsta-Hållsta connector. It hands off to 24:2 at Hållsta and the 24:1-24:3 branch eventually reaches the main trail at Svalboviken, but 24:2/24:3, Skjulsta/Karl IX canal, Vilstarundan, and parking connectors should remain separate from the core 24:1 line.

OSM relation 9631287 is topologically continuous and shares its Hållsta endpoint node with Stage 24:2 relation 9631288, but member order is not start-to-end; route drawing should use the local ordered GeoJSON/graph traversal rather than raw relation order.

Official fault section showed no reported faults during the 2026-04-27 research pass, but the same official stage text flags the Piltorp/Dalkarlstorp spring as unavailable since 2025-05. Older AllTrails blowdown reports from 2023 appear stale after later 2024/2025 good/fair condition reports.

Eskilstuna announced 2026 Vilsta friluftsområde development and traffic-safety works near Vilstavägen, including local narrowings and changed motor access; this may affect local car access/parking approaches without implying the trail is closed.

Route character is easy-to-moderate lowland hiking: Vilsta reserve paths and exercise tracks, Skjulsta/Karl IX canal side context, old mine hole, Uvberget hillfort/viewpoint, small hilly/rocky terrain toward Dalkarlstorp, Skogstorp-Stenkvista road crossing, Granstusjön, Dansberget, then easier path to Hållstavägen. Older reports mention wet, rocky, mosquito-heavy or awkward conditions around Granstusjön/Dansberget after rain.

Vilsta nature reserve rules apply near the start: fires only at designated places, no damaging trees/plants/geological features, motor vehicles only on roads/parking, riding only on marked riding trails/roads, and organized camps/competitions require consultation with Eskilstuna municipality.

Dogs must be leashed in Vilsta nature reserve and signed exercise tracks. Eskilstuna local rules also restrict dogs at municipal bathing places during the summer bathing season except designated dog bathing areas.

Ordinary one-night tenting was not found to be explicitly banned in Vilsta reserve, but do not treat the friluftsområde as a wild-camp spot. Use durable, discreet sites away from homes, crops, riding routes, facility grounds, and sensitive areas; organized group camps require consultation.

facilities.name: Skogstorp road-crossing services

facilities.name: Hållsta stage endpoint, no parking
facilities.description: Official shared 24:1 endpoint and 24:2 start near Hållstavägen. Stage 24:2 says no parking at the stage start; use bus/road-walk planning or other legal parking.

facilities.name: Åläng closer bus context
facilities.description: Closer Hållsta-side bus context west of the trail endpoint. Verify live Sörmlandstrafiken; current public map shows line 19 Hållsta-Bälgviken while older official text may still say bus 9.

facilities.name: Hållsta village bus stops
facilities.description: Secondary Hållsta village bus access, farther west/northwest of the trail endpoint. Night bus 65 and line 19 context must be verified live before relying on it.

facilities.name: Hållsta village services
facilities.description: Small off-route Hållsta village service context such as pizzeria/fuel/kiosk west of the trail endpoint; do not infer toilet, tap, groceries, or trailhead service, and verify opening hours.

facilities.name: Hållsta badplats side facility
facilities.description: Off-route village bathing place in an old gravel pit with sand beach, jetty, grill place, seating, toilet and dog-bathing context. Park only where signed and do not treat lake water as drinking water.
